answer: Remote hardware attestation deters Sybil attacks by requiring agents to sign messages with keys sealed inside secure enclaves. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of buying dedicated silicon per identity, bridging the canyon between virtual software and physical chips. These attestations form the structural timber of consensus, ensuring an expired key becomes an inert relic. However, side-channel exploits and leaked root keys allow attackers to forge attestations on unsecured chips.
